message: Hi, I'm a student with a full stack certification background. My overall academic average is 76.2% in an IT/computer-science degree. I'm interested in programming and system developer. I want to become a Technical Engineer.

uncertainty_notes: budget maximum per year is unknown.
Mobility preference is unknown (defaulting to open_domestic).

reflection_note: The original shortlist contained a hard violation (PR0144 grade requirement). I dropped it immediately. PR0198 was kept because of its high employability and location, but I swapped in PR0139 to provide an alternative option with similar strengths (high salary/good placement) while offering geographical diversity (Delhi vs Bengaluru). The final list prioritizes technical depth (PR0186), financial safety (PR0058), and strong career outcomes (PR0198, PR0139).
explanation:
Halcyon Institute of Technology
This program is recommended because its focus on networking and cloud technologies aligns well with your goal of becoming a system developer. You meet the admission criteria, as it requires a CS background and has a minimum grade requirement of 70%, which is below your current 76.2%. The tuition cost is relatively low at $2050 per year, but the main trade-off to consider is that its placement rate (83%) is not the highest among the options.

Stanmore School of Engineering
This MCA program is a strong fit for your technical goals, combining software engineering with data science analytics. It has the lowest annual tuition cost ($1350) and requires a CS background, which matches your academic history. While it offers an 83% placement rate, the primary trade-off here is that its median starting salary of $14,869 is the lowest among all programs listed.

Northgate Institute of Technology
This program stands out due to its exceptional metrics, boasting a 95% placement rate and the highest median starting salary ($21,062). The curriculum focuses on software engineering, which supports your technical career goal. However, the main trade-off is that the minimum required grade percentage (80%) is higher than your current academic standing of 76.2%.

Quilon University
This MSc program offers a high median starting salary ($20,639) and a strong placement rate of 89%, making it highly attractive for employability. The main trade-off to consider is the combination of its highest tuition fee at $4200 per year and a minimum grade requirement (81%) that exceeds your current academic percentage.
